# MID PENN BANK PROVIDES MORE THAN $1 MILLION IN FINANCING TO SUPPORT NORTH CITY CONGRESS EXPANSION IN PHILADELPHIA


Posted on Nov 19th, 2026


Millersburg, Pa. – November 19, 2026. Mid Penn Bank (the “Bank”), a wholly-owned subsidiary of Mid Penn Bancorp, Inc. (“Mid Penn”) (NASDAQ: MPB), has provided over $1 million in financing to North City Congress (“NCC”), a Philadelphia-based nonprofit organization, to support the acquisition of a property in Philadelphia’s Mount Airy neighborhood and the expansion of its behavioral health and community-based services.


Led by Mid Penn Bank First Senior Vice President and Central Philadelphia Regional President Abe Ibrahim, the financing includes a $787,500 commercial mortgage for the property acquisition and a $250,000 commercial line of credit to support working capital needs. Located at 6829 Germantown Ave., the property was acquired following NCC’s selection through a request for proposals process to provide applied behavior analysis (“ABA”) early childhood education services for neurodivergent children. The new location is expected to begin providing services in early to mid-2027. The additional financing will support NCC’s operational infrastructure and capacity expansion as the organization continues to develop its programs and services.


“North City Congress has been a part of the Philadelphia community for more than 60 years, and we’re proud to support this next step in bringing more services to children and families,” Ibrahim said. “As Mid Penn Bank expands its presence in Philadelphia, we’re focused on building relationships with organizations like NCC and providing the funding and support they need to continue serving the people who rely on them.”


Founded in 1965, NCC is a social services and licensed behavioral health organization that provides a range of programs to Philadelphia residents. Its longstanding services include youth enrichment activities and an older adult activity center that promotes social engagement and wellness. In recent years, NCC has expanded its services through additional licensure and program development to include three specialized areas of care: intensive behavioral health services, outpatient behavioral health, and home care for eligible veterans. These programs provide applied behavior analysis and mobile therapy for neurodivergent children and young adults under 21, outpatient and mobile therapy and psychiatric care for individuals experiencing behavioral or emotional challenges, and in-home assistance for eligible veterans.


“As we expand our reach to include ABA-focused early childhood education, finding a location that meets the needs of our programs is an important part of being able to serve more children and families,” said Joan Hardaway, CEO of North City Congress. “With Mid Penn Bank’s support, we’ve been able to purchase this property and make plans for the services we’ll provide there. We’re grateful for their willingness to work with us and understand what we’re trying to accomplish.”


The financing follows Mid Penn Bank’s recent support of a Turn the Key affordable housing development in Philadelphia’s Brewerytown neighborhood. The Bank provided approximately $1.9 million in construction financing for the development of 10 single-family homes for income-qualified, first-time homebuyers.

### About Mid Penn Bank

Mid Penn offers a comprehensive portfolio of financial products and services to meet the banking needs of the communities it serves.
